props.gloss_en: the mishna: the bank of a pit and a boulder ten high and four wide -- one who takes from them or places on them is liable
R' Yochanan: a pit and its bank join to make up the ten
the baraita: a pit in the public domain ten deep and four wide -- one may not draw from it on Shabbat unless a partition ten handbreadths high was made for it
the baraita: and one may not drink from it on Shabbat unless he put his head and most of his body into it
the baraita: and a pit and its bank join to make up the ten
horn 1: a column in the public domain ten high and four wide, one threw and it landed on it -- the lifting was forbidden and the placing was forbidden [so liable]
horn 2: or perhaps, since it comes from an exempt place -- not [liable]
Rav Mordekhai: you all spit the same spittle
Rav Mordekhai: perhaps the mishna is of a needle
horn 1: a wall in the public domain ten high, not four wide, enclosing a karmelit and making it a private domain -- since it is not four wide, it is an exempt place
horn 2: or perhaps, since it made [the karmelit] a private domain, it is as though filled
Rav, and R' Yochanan: [such] a wall -- one threw and it landed on it: liable
dilemma 1, horn 1: a nine-deep pit, one lifted a clod from it and completed it to ten -- lifting the object and making the partition together: liable
dilemma 1, horn 2: or not liable
dilemma 2 (if not liable in 1): a ten-deep pit, one put a clod into it and reduced it -- placing the object and removing the partition together: liable
dilemma 2, horn 2: or not liable

the mishna (quoted): one who throws four cubits at a wall -- above ten handbreadths, like throwing into the air; below ten, like throwing onto the ground; and one who throws four cubits onto the ground is liable
R' Yochanan: it is of a fat fig-cake that we learned [it]
Rava's dilemma, horn 1: one threw a board with an object on it -- since they come together, it is like placing the object and making the partition together
horn 2: or perhaps, since it cannot but rise a little and then come to rest, it is like making the partition and [then] placing the object
Rava: it is obvious to me -- water on top of water, that is its resting
Rava: a nut on water -- that is not its resting
Rava's dilemma, horn 1: a nut in a vessel floating on water -- we follow the nut, and it is at rest
horn 2: or perhaps we follow the vessel, and it is not at rest
Rava: oil on wine is the dispute of R' Yochanan ben Nuri and the Rabbis
the mishna: oil floating on wine, and a tevul yom touched the oil -- he disqualified only the oil
R' Yochanan ben Nuri: the two are a connection to each other
Abaye: a pit in the public domain ten deep and eight wide, one threw a mat into it -- liable
Abaye: [if] he divided it with the mat -- exempt
stam, per Abaye, for whom it is obvious that a mat nullifies the partition: all the more so a clod nullifies the partition
stam, per R' Yochanan, who is in doubt about a clod: a mat obviously does not nullify the partition
Abaye: a pit in the public domain ten deep and four wide, full of water, one threw into it -- liable
Abaye: full of produce, one threw into it -- exempt
what is the reason? water does not nullify the partition; produce nullifies the partition
the baraita: one who throws from the sea to the street, or from the street to the sea -- exempt
R' Shimon: if the place where he threw is ten deep and four wide -- liable

questions.gloss_en: Rav Mordekhai's iba'ya: a column in the public domain ten high and four wide, one threw and it landed on it -- what is the law? (the mishna's resolution is rebuffed; the text records no answer)

R' Yochanan: a ten-deep pit reduced by putting in a clod -- liable or not? (the stam's תיפשוט is rebuffed; unresolved)
Rava: a board thrown with an object on it, landing on stakes -- placement-with-partition, or partition-then-placement? teiku
